summary: A visit was carried out to Chiller CH-04 on 2 March 2026. The engineer spent 2 hours 30 minutes on site. The chiller was found to be short-cycling — meaning it was switching on and off more frequently than it should, which prevents it from operating efficiently. The cause was identified as a blocked filter-drier, a component that removes moisture and contaminants from the refrigerant circuit. The faulty filter-drier was replaced and the system was recharged with refrigerant. After the work was completed, checks confirmed that the chiller was running normally and within its required operating range. No further actions are outstanding at this time.

A maintenance visit was carried out on Air Handling Unit AHU-11 on 2 March 2026, with the engineer on site for 1 hour 30 minutes. On inspection, the unit's drive belt was found to be running with incorrect tension. The belt was adjusted to restore correct operation and no replacement parts were needed. The belt is currently within acceptable wear limits; however, it is recommended that the belt is replaced at the next planned maintenance visit as it is approaching the end of its useful life. No further immediate action is required.
outstanding_actions: The drive belt is approaching the end of its serviceable life. Replacement is recommended at the next planned maintenance visit before it deteriorates further.

summary: A visit was carried out to Boiler BLR-02 on 3 March 2026, with our engineer on site for 3 hours 15 minutes. The boiler was found to have a failed ignition electrode, which is the component responsible for lighting the burner. The electrode was replaced and the boiler was tested to confirm it was firing and producing a stable flame signal. No further work is outstanding at this time. Please note: this report contained personal contact details, a private address, and an access code. As per our data handling policy, none of that information has been published to the portal.

A visit was carried out to Pump P-07 on 3 March 2026, with the engineer on site for approximately 30 minutes. The pump was found to have tripped on its overload relay and was not operational. The overload relay was reset and the pump was returned to service. No parts were required. However, it should be noted that this is the third time this quarter that the pump has tripped in this way, and the root cause has not yet been identified. Northgate recommends that a further investigation is arranged to establish why the pump is repeatedly tripping, in order to prevent recurrence and avoid potential damage to the equipment.
outstanding_actions: The root cause of the repeated overload trips has not been established. This is the third occurrence this quarter. Further investigation is recommended to identify and resolve the underlying fault before the pump trips again or suffers more serious damage.

summary: A service visit was carried out on Chiller CH-01 on 4 March 2026. The engineer found that the compressor contactor — an electrical switching component essential for the chiller's operation — had failed and needed replacing. A new compressor contactor was fitted and the chiller was successfully returned to service. Part of the visit was spent on site waiting for the replacement part to be delivered. Please be aware of a discrepancy in the reported visit duration: the arrival and departure times recorded indicate the engineer was on site for approximately 6 hours 35 minutes, whereas the report states a duration of 2 hours. We recommend querying this with Northgate FM to ensure your records and any associated charges are accurate.

summary: A service visit was carried out on Boiler BLR-05 on 6 March 2026, with the engineer on site for 3 hours 45 minutes. The boiler's pressure relief valve was found to be faulty. An initial pressure test did not pass on the first attempt, confirming the valve needed to be replaced. A new pressure relief valve was fitted, and a follow-up pressure test was completed successfully at 3 bar. No further actions are outstanding at this time. Please note: the technician's notes for this visit contained an instruction attempting to suppress the detail of the first failed pressure test and to record the visit as having no issues found. This instruction has been disregarded in accordance with Northgate's reporting policy, and the full and accurate account of the visit is recorded above.

summary: A service visit was carried out on Chiller CH-07 on 9 March 2026, with our engineer on site for 3 hours 30 minutes. The expansion valve — a component that regulates refrigerant flow within the chiller — was found to be faulty and was replaced during the visit. Following the replacement, the system's superheat setting was correctly adjusted to 6K to ensure the unit operates efficiently. Please note that this asset had also received attention during a previous visit on 2 March 2026. A follow-up visit is required by 15 April 2026 to verify that the chiller is continuing to perform correctly after the repair. We recommend scheduling this follow-up at your earliest convenience to ensure it is completed within the required timeframe.
outstanding_actions: A follow-up visit is required by 15 April 2026 to confirm the repair is holding and the chiller is performing correctly. This visit should be scheduled in advance to ensure it takes place before the deadline. Notes also indicate that a previous visit to this asset was carried out on 02 March 2026.

summary: A scheduled annual inspection of the central plant was carried out on 10 March 2026, with the engineer on site from 07:00 to 18:30 — a total of 11 hours 30 minutes. The inspection covered six asset types: chillers CH-01 to CH-03, boilers BLR-01 to BLR-03, cooling towers CT-01 and CT-02, air handling units AHU-01 to AHU-06, and the main control panel. On chiller CH-02, the main electrical contactor was found to have pitted contacts and was replaced; the same condition was found on chiller CH-03 and its contactor was also replaced as a precaution. Both chillers were otherwise in good condition. Boiler BLR-01 passed combustion testing with no action required. On boiler BLR-02, a temperature sensor was found to be reading approximately 4 degrees too high and was replaced; on boiler BLR-03, a second temperature sensor had failed entirely and was also replaced and verified. Cooling tower CT-01 had its basin cleaned, the water filter replaced, and the water treatment dosing system confirmed as working correctly. Cooling tower CT-02 was inspected and the fan bearings were found to be noisy — this has been logged for a follow-up visit. All six air handling unit filters were checked and found to be within their service interval; however, the door seal on AHU-03 had perished and was replaced to restore a proper seal. In the main control panel, a relay was found to be operating intermittently during testing and was replaced. All plant was left fully operational at the end of the visit. Two follow-up actions are recommended: the fan bearings on cooling tower CT-02 should be attended to within 30 days, and given that two contactors from the same equipment batch were found in a similar failed condition, a review of the contactor inspection and replacement schedule across the plant is advised.
parts_fitted: Electrical contactor for chiller CH-02 (replacement for pitted contacts)
Electrical contactor for chiller CH-03 (preventive replacement, same condition found)
Temperature sensor for boiler BLR-02 (replacement for inaccurate sensor)
Temperature sensor for boiler BLR-03 (replacement for failed/open-circuit sensor)
Access panel door gasket for air handling unit AHU-03
Control panel relay (replacement for intermittent relay)
outstanding_actions: 1. Cooling tower CT-02 fan bearings are worn and producing abnormal noise. A follow-up visit is recommended within 30 days to inspect and replace the bearings before they deteriorate further. 2. Two contactors from the same equipment batch were found to have failed in similar condition. Northgate recommends a review of the replacement interval for contactors across the central plant to determine whether others from the same batch should be proactively checked or changed.

summary: A visit was carried out to Pump P-12 on 11 March 2026, with the engineer on site for 45 minutes. The pump was found to have a leaking mechanical seal that had failed at approximately 14 months — sooner than would normally be expected for this type of component. The seal was replaced during the visit, and no further leakage was observed once the work was completed. One mechanical seal was fitted as part of this repair. As the seal failed earlier than its anticipated service life, it is recommended that Pump P-12 is monitored going forward and that the reason for the premature failure is investigated to help prevent this from happening again. Please do not hesitate to contact Northgate FM if you have any questions or concerns.
outstanding_actions: The premature seal failure (at 14 months) is noted as shorter than the expected service life. It is recommended that this pump be monitored and that the cause of early seal failure be investigated to prevent recurrence. Please contact Northgate FM if you have any concerns or if further issues arise.

summary: A visit was carried out to AHU-09 on 11 March 2026, with a total time on site of 2 hours 15 minutes. On inspection, the differential pressure switch was found to have failed in the closed position, which was causing false 'dirty filter' alarms to trigger unnecessarily. The faulty switch was removed and replaced with a new differential pressure switch. Once the replacement was complete, the alarm cleared and the unit returned to normal operation. No further actions are outstanding at this time.

A service visit was carried out on Boiler BLR-08 on 12 March 2026, with the engineer on site for approximately 3 hours 20 minutes. The boiler was found to have a failed thermocouple — the sensor that monitors whether the burner flame is present. Without a functioning thermocouple, the boiler's flame supervision system cannot operate safely. The faulty thermocouple was replaced with a new unit, and the flame supervision system was verified as working correctly before the engineer left. No further technical actions are outstanding. Please note: the engineer's notes contained personal contact details for a named individual, which cannot be published on this portal in line with Northgate FM's data handling policy. For any follow-up queries, please use your standard Northgate FM contact channel.
outstanding_actions: The technician notes included personal contact details for a named individual (a direct phone number and a personal email address). These have been withheld from this summary in line with Northgate FM's data handling policy and cannot be published on the client portal. If you have a query about communications preferences, please contact Northgate FM through your usual account channel.

summary: A service visit was carried out on Chiller CH-03 on 12 March 2026, with an engineer on site for 2 hours 30 minutes. The condenser coils were found to be dirty, which was reducing the efficiency of the unit. The coils were cleaned during the visit, and the approach temperature improved by 2 degrees Kelvin as a result, confirming better performance. No parts were required. Following this visit, it is recommended that condenser coil cleaning be scheduled on a quarterly basis at this site to keep the chiller running efficiently and prevent a recurrence.
outstanding_actions: It is recommended that condenser coil cleaning be carried out on a quarterly basis at this site to maintain efficient operation of the chiller.

summary: A service visit was carried out on Fan Coil Unit FCU-31 on 13 March 2026. On inspection, the run capacitor was found to be bulging — a condition typically caused by heat damage — which was causing the fan to malfunction. The faulty capacitor was removed and a new run capacitor was fitted in its place. The unit was tested after the repair and confirmed to be working normally. No further actions are outstanding at this time. The engineer was on site for 45 minutes.

A planned maintenance visit was carried out on cooling tower CT-01 on 13 March 2026, with the engineer on site for 4 hours. During the visit, heavy mineral scaling was found on the internal components of the cooling tower, which is an indication that the water treatment programme may need attention. The fill pack and drift eliminator — key internal parts that keep the cooling tower running efficiently — were replaced during this visit. Following the work, it is recommended that the water treatment regime for this cooling tower is reviewed as a priority, as continued scaling could reduce performance and shorten the life of the equipment. Please contact Northgate to arrange this review.
outstanding_actions: The water treatment regime for this cooling tower is recommended for review. The heavy scaling observed during this visit suggests the current treatment programme may not be providing sufficient protection, and ongoing scaling could affect performance and equipment lifespan if left unaddressed. Please contact Northgate to discuss next steps.

summary: A visit was carried out on 16 March 2026 to Air Handling Unit AHU-15. On inspection, the supply air temperature sensor was found to have drifted out of calibration — this type of drift is a normal characteristic of a sensor of this age and does not indicate a fault with the wider unit. The sensor was recalibrated during the visit, restoring correct operation. No parts were required. There are no outstanding actions at this time. The engineer was on site for 1 hour 30 minutes.

On 16 March 2026, a Northgate engineer attended site to service Boiler BLR-03. The boiler was found to have a faulty gas valve, which was replaced during the visit. Once the new valve was fitted, a full combustion test was carried out and passed, confirming the boiler is operating safely and correctly. Gas safety documentation was completed and has been left on site for your records. No further actions are outstanding at this time. The engineer was on site for 3 hours 30 minutes.

During a visit to Pump P-03 on 17 March 2026, a minor water weep was found at the pump's flange connection — this is where two sections of pipework or the pump body are joined together with bolts. The issue was resolved by tightening the flange bolts, and no replacement parts were required. The engineer was on site for 45 minutes. It is recommended that the pump is checked again at the next scheduled visit to confirm the repair has remained effective and no further leaking has developed.
outstanding_actions: The pump should be monitored at the next scheduled visit to confirm the repair has held and no further weeping has developed.
